title: A clearer handoff, from request to follow-up
environment: Fictional Salesforce UAT sandbox — no live org linked
intro: A small service team wants every customer request to reach the right person, with enough context to act. Use this sample pack to explore how structured UAT feedback works.
instructions: This is an example test specification, not evidence of a configured Salesforce implementation. A delivery team would configure and validate the sandbox before inviting testers.
For a real UAT cycle, follow each scenario in the agreed test environment. Record what happened and reference evidence in the approved project channel.
Export your feedback before leaving. Nothing you type is submitted to the delivery team automatically.

stories.title: Capture a useful customer request
stories.objective: As a service coordinator, I want a complete request so that the delivery team can assess it without chasing missing information.

cases.title: Create a request with clear customer context
preconditions: An active fictional Account named Northstar Services exists.
The tester has the agreed Service Coordinator permissions.
steps: Open the agreed Customer Requests entry point.
Create a request for Northstar Services: “Review weekend support coverage”.
Enter the description: “Confirm the service options and coverage available for weekend support.” Set priority to Normal and save.
cases.expectedResult: The request saves once, receives a reference, and displays the correct Account, description, priority and initial status.
cases.testData: Account: Northstar Services; request: Review weekend support coverage. All data is fictional.

cases.title: Explain what is missing before saving
preconditions: The request form is available to the tester.
steps: Leave the required Subject field empty and attempt to save.
Enter “Review weekend support coverage” and complete the remaining required fields. Save again.
cases.expectedResult: The first attempt shows a clear required-field message without creating a request. After correction, exactly one request is saved.
cases.testData: Use a new sample request so existing results are not changed.

stories.title: Give follow-up a clear owner
stories.objective: As a service coordinator, I want an authorised specialist to find and act on their assigned work.

cases.title: Assign work and open it as the specialist
preconditions: Fictional test user Alex Morgan has the approved specialist role.
Separate authorised test sessions are available.
steps: As the coordinator, create a follow-up task for the request: “Clarify weekend coverage”.
Assign it to Alex Morgan with an agreed future due date and save.
Open the separate specialist session. Find and open the task and its related request.
cases.expectedResult: Alex sees the assigned task, due date and request context. The coordinator’s and specialist’s access matches the agreed acceptance criteria. A successful save alone does not prove the specialist can open the record.
cases.testData: Assignee: Alex Morgan; due date: choose a future business day in the UAT cycle.
